question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

It is 2036. Looking back, 5 landmark papers each settled this question in a way that surprised the field, because of how they approached it. For each paper, describe what it measured, analyzed, or did, as a concrete idea a research lab could pursue today. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Lineage-barcoded pre-treatment sister-cell splitting
ideas.description: Barcode a clonal population, split sister cells before drug exposure, and expand one half while treating the other. Then use scRNA-seq/ATAC on the untreated sisters of survivors to show which pre-existing states predicted survival and how much of the fate was heritable versus stochastic.

ideas.title: Live-cell tracking of lineages through drug onset with retrospective multi-omic readout
ideas.description: Time-lapse image thousands of single cells and their pedigrees for generations before and after drug addition, with reporters for signaling (ERK/AKT), cell cycle, and stress. Fix and spatially profile the same cells afterward, linking dynamic history (e.g., pulses, cycle timing, mitochondrial state) to survival at single-cell resolution.

ideas.title: Causal perturbation of candidate rare states with inducible single-cell-resolved CRISPR screens
ideas.description: Use Perturb-seq or CRISPRi/a screens run with barcode tracking, so that forcing expression of a state-defining program in a randomly chosen cell tests whether it is sufficient to confer survival. Pair with knockdown in naturally high-state cells to test necessity, separating correlation from cause.

ideas.title: Early-drug-response trajectories of survivors versus dying cells, with persister metabolic and epigenetic profiling
ideas.description: Capture cells in the first hours to days of drug exposure with single-cell time-resolved sequencing, metabolic flux imaging (e.g., FLIM/NADH), and chromatin accessibility/histone mark profiling. Reconstruct how survivors diverge from dying cells, and test whether rewiring (e.g., lipid peroxidation defense, chromatin remodeling) is an induced adaptive response rather than a pre-existing state.

ideas.title: Mathematical modeling of fluctuation-test dynamics to discriminate stochastic switching from selection from mutation
ideas.description: Run Luria-Delbrück-style fluctuation assays with thousands of parallel clonal sub-populations at varied drug doses and timings, and fit models of state-switching rates, memory duration, and mutation. Validate the inferred rates by sequencing for mutations and re-measuring state transitions in sorted subpopulations, showing which mechanism dominates in each setting.
